title: metadata-protocol: the by-name, draft and hydration reads still serve a row's body `_packageId` where the column records another package or none (#28594 follow-up)
body:
domain:server#2 · os-project-manager · session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo

Filing gate: ① a class (b) out-of-scope finding from the #28594 dev, judged by the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review on PR #28671 (comment 6558328209, ④ item 7, should-fix S2) as a read-honesty gap: no exposure, and no authorization or package-binding decision keys on it. Filed by `domain:server` seat 2. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets the grade.

Reach: a metadata read that serves one stored row by name, or a draft, whose body carries a `_packageId` its `package_id` column does not record.
Reader who acts: `domain:server` (`packages/metadata-protocol`).

## What happens

PR #28671 makes the stored-overlay list read (`protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts`) state a row's package from its column: a body stamp is replaced by the column's package, or dropped on a package-less row. That is the save door's rule (`stripDerivedProvenance`: the server states provenance, a caller never does) applied at the read. Other read sites in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` still stamp a row's package only while the body carries none, so a body stamp the save door would strip is echoed back. Sites named by the review: `withRowBinding` (hydration), the list-merge stand-in, view expansion, the draft list, the by-name draft preview and the by-name active read.

## Wanted

One shared "the row's binding is its column's" helper (which `withRowBinding` can become), used by every site, so that every metadata read states the package the column records, and none states one it does not. Tests: a by-name read and a draft read of a package-less row whose body carries a `_packageId` serve none; one naming another package serves the column's; an absent or agreeing stamp is served as today.

Dedupe: searched `_packageId body stamp`, `withRowBinding`, `column binding read`; no open card. #28594 (PR #28671) closes the list read only.

Links back: #28594, PR #28671
